input: Look into surrogacy agencies and initial consultations

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether the user is an intended parent or a prospective surrogate completely changes which agencies, criteria, and consultation types are relevant.
They may want a broad overview of many agencies or a deep dive into a short list — this determines how much research to do before moving to consultations.
Geographic location (country, state/province) heavily affects which agencies are legally permitted to operate, and what surrogacy laws apply.
Surrogacy agency fees vary enormously; knowing the budget shapes which agencies are realistic options to investigate.
Whether they prefer in-person, phone, or virtual consultations affects which agencies are shortlistable and how quickly they can get started.
Some people prioritise agency size, success rates, LGBTQ+ experience, faith alignment, or domestic vs. international matching — knowing priorities narrows the field.
Understanding what a successful research phase looks like (e.g., a shortlist of 3 agencies, one booked consultation, a comparison document) defines when this task is done.

gold.taskTitle: Research surrogacy agencies and book initial consultations
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to explore surrogacy agencies and arrange first consultations, likely as an early step in pursuing surrogacy as intended parents or as a surrogate.

questions.title: Are you pursuing surrogacy as an intended parent or a surrogate?
questions.description: Clarifies the user's role, which determines the entire direction of agency research and consultation focus.

questions.title: Which country and region are you based in?
questions.description: Location determines legal frameworks, agency availability, and jurisdiction-specific requirements.

questions.title: How many agencies do you want to research before consulting?
questions.description: Defines the breadth of the research phase — a quick shortlist vs. a comprehensive market scan.

questions.title: What is your approximate budget for agency fees?
questions.description: Agency costs range from tens to hundreds of thousands; budget filters out unrealistic options early.

questions.title: What qualities matter most to you in an agency?
questions.description: Surfaces key priorities such as LGBTQ+ experience, success rates, faith alignment, or domestic vs. international matching.

questions.title: Do you prefer virtual, phone, or in-person consultations?
questions.description: Consultation format affects which agencies are shortlistable and how quickly appointments can be scheduled.

questions.title: What does the end of this research phase look like for you?
questions.description: Defines the success criteria — e.g., a comparison document, a shortlist of agencies, or one consultation booked.
